title: Granular License Generator Questionnaire
description: A comprehensive 300+ question questionnaire for generating precise, granular software licenses.

questions.title: Who holds the copyright for this software?
questions.description: Identify the primary copyright holder(s) of the software being licensed. This determines who has the legal authority to grant license rights.
questions.tooltip: The copyright holder is the legal owner of the intellectual property rights in the software.
questions.help_text: If multiple parties contributed, select the appropriate option and list all holders.
questions.legal_implications: Incorrect copyright attribution can void the license and expose parties to infringement claims.

options.label: Individual developer
options.description: A single person holds the copyright

options.label: Organization or company
options.description: A legal entity holds the copyright

options.label: Joint copyright holders
options.description: Multiple parties share copyright ownership

options.label: Public domain dedication
options.description: The work is placed in the public domain

questions.title: Are there multiple copyright holders?
questions.description: If more than one person or entity contributed copyrightable code, all holders must be identified and their consent obtained.
questions.tooltip: Joint copyright requires agreement from all holders to modify license terms.
questions.help_text: List every individual or entity that contributed original code.
questions.legal_implications: Failure to obtain consent from all joint holders can result in an invalid license.

questions.title: Can ownership of this software be transferred?
questions.description: Determine whether copyright ownership can be assigned or transferred to another party in the future.
questions.tooltip: Ownership transfer (assignment) requires explicit written consent under most jurisdictions.
questions.help_text: Some open-source licenses prohibit or restrict ownership transfer.
questions.legal_implications: Without explicit transfer provisions, ownership transfer may be legally ambiguous.

questions.title: Are there existing ownership claims or liens on this software?
questions.description: Disclose any third-party claims, liens, or encumbrances that may affect the software's ownership chain.
questions.tooltip: Undisclosed claims can result in legal disputes after license grants.
questions.help_text: This includes pending litigation, inherited claims from acquired code, and contractual obligations.
questions.legal_implications: Concealing existing claims may constitute misrepresentation and void the license agreement.

questions.title: Is this a work made for hire?
questions.description: If the software was created by employees within the scope of their employment, the employer typically owns the copyright automatically.
questions.tooltip: Work-for-hire status affects who holds initial copyright and who can license it.
questions.help_text: Consult legal counsel if the employment relationship or contractor status is ambiguous.
questions.legal_implications: Mischaracterizing employment status can create disputed ownership and invalidate license grants.

questions.title: Does this license explicitly address copyright?
questions.description: Decide whether the generated license should include an explicit copyright grant clause separate from the patent grant.
questions.tooltip: An explicit copyright clause clarifies what rights are being licensed under copyright law.
questions.help_text: Most licenses include a copyright grant to avoid ambiguity.
questions.legal_implications: Without an explicit copyright clause, licensees may lack clear authorization to exercise copyright-protected rights.

questions.title: What copyright notice format should be used?
questions.description: Specify the format for the copyright notice that must accompany the software and derivative works.
questions.tooltip: A consistent copyright notice format helps maintain proper attribution chains.
questions.help_text: The standard format is: Copyright [year] [holder name].

recommended_answer.Text: Copyright (c) {year} {holder}

questions.legal_implications: An improperly formatted notice may not satisfy statutory requirements in some jurisdictions.

questions.title: Must copyright registration be obtained?
questions.description: Determine whether users or downstream distributors are required to register the copyright in their jurisdiction.
questions.tooltip: Copyright registration is not required for protection in many countries but provides legal advantages in others.
questions.help_text: In the US, registration is required before filing an infringement lawsuit.
questions.legal_implications: Requiring registration in jurisdictions where it is optional may impose unnecessary burdens on licensees.

questions.title: Can copyright be waived or dedicated to the public domain?
questions.description: Choose whether to allow the copyright holder to fully waive their rights, placing the software in the public domain.
questions.tooltip: Public domain dedication means anyone can use the software without any license conditions.
questions.help_text: Tools like CC0 or the Unlicense can facilitate public domain dedication.
questions.legal_implications: Public domain status is not recognized in all jurisdictions; a permissive license may be more effective.

options.label: License only (retain copyright)
options.description: Keep copyright and grant rights via license

options.label: Public domain dedication
options.description: Fully waive all rights

options.label: Both options available
options.description: Allow choice between license and public domain

questions.title: How long should the copyright protection period be?
questions.description: Specify the intended duration of copyright protection, although in most jurisdictions duration is determined by law.
questions.tooltip: Copyright duration is typically set by statute (e.g., life + 70 years in the US and EU).
questions.help_text: While parties cannot typically shorten statutory copyright terms, the license duration can be limited.
questions.legal_implications: Attempting to modify statutory copyright duration may be unenforceable in many jurisdictions.

options.label: Statutory duration (default)
options.description: Follow the copyright term prescribed by law

options.label: License limited to specific period
options.description: The license grants rights for a fixed term only

options.label: Perpetual license
options.description: License rights extend for as long as copyright exists

questions.title: Is commercial use of this software permitted?
questions.description: Determine whether licensees are allowed to use this software for commercial purposes, including selling products or services built with it.
questions.tooltip: Commercial use typically means any use intended for or resulting in commercial advantage or monetary compensation.
questions.help_text: Restricting commercial use may reduce adoption but can protect revenue streams.
questions.legal_implications: Vague commercial use restrictions can lead to disputes about what constitutes commercial use.

options.label: Permitted without restrictions
options.description: Commercial use is fully allowed

options.label: Permitted with conditions
options.description: Commercial use allowed under specific terms

options.label: Not permitted
options.description: Commercial use is prohibited

options.label: Requires separate license
options.description: Commercial users must obtain a commercial license

questions.title: Does commercial use require a separate license?
questions.description: If commercial use is conditional, determine whether a separate commercial license must be obtained.
questions.tooltip: A dual-license model separates open-source and commercial terms.
questions.help_text: This is common in open-core business models where the core is open source but commercial features require a paid license.
questions.legal_implications: Clear separation between free and commercial tiers prevents confusion and potential breach claims.

questions.title: What revenue threshold triggers commercial license requirements?
questions.description: Set the annual revenue threshold above which a commercial license is required. This allows small businesses and startups to use the software freely.
questions.tooltip: Revenue thresholds help protect small entities while monetizing larger users.
questions.help_text: Common thresholds range from $50,000 to $1,000,000 in annual revenue.
questions.legal_implications: Thresholds must be clearly defined and consistently enforced to maintain legal validity.

questions.title: What commercial use restrictions apply?
questions.description: Select all restrictions that apply to commercial use of this software.
questions.tooltip: Specific restrictions help tailor the license to your business needs.
questions.help_text: Select only the restrictions that are necessary for your licensing model.
questions.legal_implications: Overly broad restrictions may render the license unenforceable or deter potential users.

options.label: Attribution required
options.description: Must credit the original author in commercial products

options.label: Revenue sharing
options.description: Must share a percentage of revenue

options.label: Source disclosure required
options.description: Must disclose source code for commercial products

options.label: Notification required
options.description: Must notify the licensor of commercial use

questions.title: Should a dual-licensing model be offered?
questions.description: Determine whether the software should be available under both an open-source license and a commercial license simultaneously.
questions.tooltip: Dual licensing allows users to choose between an open-source license (with copyleft obligations) and a commercial license (typically paid, without copyleft obligations).
questions.help_text: This model works best when all copyright holders agree to dual licensing.
questions.legal_implications: Dual licensing requires ownership or authorization from all copyright holders to offer both license options.

questions.title: Is use in academic or scientific research permitted?
questions.description: Determine whether the software may be used in research contexts, including experiments, publications, and academic projects.
questions.tooltip: Research use exemptions can significantly increase academic adoption.
questions.help_text: Many open-source licenses implicitly allow research use, but an explicit grant removes ambiguity.
questions.legal_implications: Restricting research use may limit academic citation and recognition of the software.

questions.title: Are research results built with this software required to be shared openly?
questions.description: Decide whether researchers using the software must publish or share their results, datasets, or findings openly.
questions.tooltip: Open science mandates can increase the impact of the software in the research community.
questions.help_text: Some funders require open-access publication; aligning the license with these requirements can be beneficial.
questions.legal_implications: Mandatory sharing requirements may conflict with institutional publication policies or funding agreements.

questions.title: Do research institutions receive special license terms?
questions.description: Determine whether accredited research institutions receive different or more permissive license terms.
questions.tooltip: Institutional exemptions can encourage wider academic adoption.
questions.help_text: Define what qualifies as a research institution (e.g., accredited universities, government labs).
questions.legal_implications: Unequal treatment of different user categories must be clearly defined to avoid discrimination claims.

questions.title: What are the publication requirements when using this software in research?
questions.description: Specify whether and how the software must be cited or acknowledged in research publications.
questions.tooltip: Publication requirements ensure the software receives proper academic credit.
questions.help_text: Standard citation formats include academic paper references, DOI links, or repository URLs.
questions.legal_implications: Publication requirements must be reasonable and not impose undue burden on researchers.

options.label: Citation required
options.description: Must cite the software in publications

options.label: Acknowledgment sufficient
options.description: A general acknowledgment is sufficient

options.label: No publication requirements
options.description: No specific publication obligations

questions.title: Is use in academic coursework and teaching permitted?
questions.description: Determine whether the software can be used in educational settings such as classrooms, homework assignments, and academic exercises.
questions.tooltip: Academic use exemptions help integrate software into curricula.
questions.help_text: This is distinct from research use; academic use focuses on teaching and learning.
questions.legal_implications: Restricting educational use may limit the software's pedagogical value and institutional adoption.

questions.title: What academic license terms should apply?
questions.description: Choose the licensing model for academic institutions using this software.
questions.tooltip: Academic licenses often offer reduced fees or more permissive terms.
questions.help_text: Consider whether students, faculty, and staff should have different access levels.
questions.legal_implications: Clearly defined academic terms prevent unauthorized commercial use under the guise of education.

options.label: Free with attribution
options.description: Free use if properly attributed

options.label: Discounted license
options.description: Reduced fee academic license

options.label: Full license applies
options.description: No special academic terms

options.label: Free for all academic use
options.description: Completely free for all academic purposes

questions.title: Can students use this software in personal projects?
questions.description: Determine whether students enrolled at academic institutions can use the software for personal, non-course-related projects.
questions.tooltip: Student personal use extends the software's reach beyond the classroom.
questions.help_text: Consider whether the student's project might later become commercial.
questions.legal_implications: Personal project use by students may blur the line between academic and commercial use over time.

questions.title: Are academic institutions required to include the license in course materials?
questions.description: Specify whether instructors must include the license text or terms when using the software in their courses.
questions.tooltip: License inclusion in course materials ensures students understand their obligations.
questions.help_text: This is especially important for courses that involve distributing modified versions of the software.
questions.legal_implications: Failure to inform students of license terms may complicate enforcement downstream.

questions.title: Does this license include an express patent grant?
questions.description: Decide whether the license should include an explicit grant of patent rights from the licensor to the licensee.
questions.tooltip: An express patent grant protects licensees from patent infringement claims by the licensor.
questions.help_text: Patent grants are common in major open-source licenses like Apache 2.0 and GPLv3.
questions.legal_implications: Without an express patent grant, licensees may be vulnerable to patent claims even if they comply with copyright terms.

questions.title: What is the scope of the patent grant?
questions.description: Define how broadly the patent rights are granted under this license.
questions.tooltip: The scope determines which patent-related activities are covered by the grant.
questions.help_text: Broader scope provides more protection to licensees but may expose the licensor to more risk.
questions.legal_implications: Narrowly scoped patent grants may leave licensees exposed in certain jurisdictions or use cases.

options.label: Worldwide, perpetual
options.description: Full global patent rights for the life of the patents

options.label: Territory-limited
options.description: Patent rights limited to specific countries or regions

options.label: Use-case limited
options.description: Patent rights limited to specific types of use

options.label: No patent grant
options.description: No patent rights are granted

questions.title: What conditions attach to the patent grant?
questions.description: Select the conditions that must be met for the patent grant to remain in effect.
questions.tooltip: Conditions on the patent grant help protect the licensor from patent aggression.
questions.help_text: Common conditions include compliance with license terms and no patent litigation against the licensor.
questions.legal_implications: Conditions that are too onerous may undermine the patent grant's value to licensees.

options.label: License compliance required
options.description: Grant only valid if licensee follows license terms

options.label: No litigation against licensor
options.description: Grant revoked if licensee sues licensor for patents

options.label: Improvement disclosure
options.description: Must disclose improvements to patented technology

options.label: No conditions
options.description: The patent grant has no conditions

questions.title: Does the license include a patent retaliation clause?
questions.description: Determine whether patent rights are automatically revoked if the licensee initiates patent litigation against the licensor.
questions.tooltip: Patent retaliation clauses deter patent aggression against the licensor and other licensees.
questions.help_text: This is a standard feature in many modern open-source licenses.
questions.legal_implications: Retaliation clauses must be carefully drafted to avoid being considered unconscionable in some jurisdictions.

questions.title: Should the patent retaliation clause be included?
questions.description: Decide whether to include a clause that terminates patent grants if the licensee sues the licensor for patent infringement.
questions.tooltip: Patent retaliation is a defensive mechanism to protect the licensor and community.
questions.help_text: This clause is recommended for projects that want to prevent patent trolling.
questions.legal_implications: The enforceability of retaliation clauses varies by jurisdiction and must be clearly drafted.

questions.title: What triggers the patent retaliation clause?
questions.description: Define the specific actions that would trigger patent rights termination.
questions.tooltip: Clear trigger conditions prevent disputes about when retaliation applies.
questions.help_text: Consider whether indirect litigation (e.g., through subsidiaries) should also trigger the clause.
questions.legal_implications: Overly broad triggers may discourage legitimate patent enforcement by licensees.

options.label: Direct patent litigation
options.description: Filing a patent lawsuit directly against the licensor

options.label: Indirect litigation
options.description: Using subsidiaries or affiliates to litigate

options.label: Patent assertion claims
options.description: Any assertion of patent rights against the licensor

options.label: Contributory infringement
options.description: Contributing to patent infringement claims against the licensor

questions.title: What is the scope of the patent retaliation?
questions.description: Determine how broadly the retaliation provisions apply when triggered.
questions.tooltip: The scope determines what rights are lost when retaliation is triggered.
questions.help_text: Consider whether to revoke all license rights or only patent-specific rights.
questions.legal_implications: Revoking more rights than necessary may be seen as disproportionate and reduce enforceability.

options.label: Patent grant only
options.description: Only patent rights are revoked; copyright license continues

options.label: All license rights
options.description: The entire license is terminated including copyright

options.label: Tiered revocation
options.description: Graduated response depending on severity

questions.title: Is there a defensive termination provision?
questions.description: Include a provision that prevents the licensor from initiating patent claims against users who comply with the license.
questions.tooltip: Defensive termination ensures the licensor does not use patents offensively against compliant users.
questions.help_text: This is sometimes called a 'patent peace' clause.
questions.legal_implications: A mutual defensive provision creates a balanced patent relationship between licensor and licensee.

questions.title: Can the software name and trademarks be used by licensees?
questions.description: Determine whether licensees are permitted to use the software's name, logos, and other trademarks.
questions.tooltip: Trademark rights are separate from copyright and are not automatically licensed.
questions.help_text: Most open-source licenses explicitly exclude trademark rights from the license grant.
questions.legal_implications: Uncontrolled trademark use can lead to brand confusion and loss of trademark protections.

questions.title: What trademark usage restrictions apply?
questions.description: Select the restrictions on how the software's trademarks may be used by licensees and third parties.
questions.tooltip: Trademark restrictions protect the brand identity of the software project.
questions.help_text: Consider both the software name and any associated logos or branding elements.
questions.legal_implications: Trademark misuse can result in 'genericide' and loss of trademark protection.

options.label: No modification of marks
options.description: Trademarks must be used exactly as provided

options.label: Attribution only
options.description: Trademarks can be used only for attribution

options.label: No use of trademarks
options.description: Trademarks may not be used at all

options.label: Approved use only
options.description: Use requires prior written approval

questions.title: Are trademarks licensed separately from the copyright?
questions.description: Clarify whether trademark rights are handled in a separate agreement from the copyright license.
questions.tooltip: Separate trademark licensing gives the licensor more control over brand usage.
questions.help_text: This is the standard approach in most major open-source projects.
questions.legal_implications: Mixing trademark and copyright terms can create confusion about what rights are actually granted.

questions.title: What are the trademark attribution requirements?
questions.description: Specify how trademark attribution should be presented when the trademarks are used with permission.
questions.tooltip: Proper trademark attribution helps maintain the distinctiveness of the marks.
questions.help_text: Trademark attribution typically uses the TM or R symbol and a statement of ownership.

recommended_answer.Text: Use of {trademark} is subject to approval. {holder} is the owner of the {trademark} trademark.

questions.legal_implications: Incorrect trademark attribution (e.g., using R for unregistered marks) can constitute false advertising.

questions.title: Must source code be disclosed when distributing the software?
questions.description: Determine whether licensees must make the source code available when they distribute the software or derivative works.
questions.tooltip: Source disclosure requirements are a hallmark of copyleft licenses.
questions.help_text: Permissive licenses typically do not require source disclosure; copyleft licenses always do.
questions.legal_implications: Failure to comply with source disclosure requirements is a material breach of copyleft licenses.

options.label: No disclosure required
options.description: Binary distribution is sufficient

options.label: Disclosure on request
options.description: Source must be provided when users request it

options.label: Disclosure required with distribution
options.description: Source must accompany every distribution

options.label: Disclosure for derivative works only
options.description: Only modified versions require source disclosure

questions.title: What triggers source code disclosure obligations?
questions.description: Define the specific scenarios that trigger source code disclosure requirements.
questions.tooltip: Different triggers create different levels of disclosure obligation.
questions.help_text: Consider whether internal distribution, SaaS hosting, or other activities should trigger disclosure.
questions.legal_implications: Unclear triggers can lead to inadvertent non-compliance with source disclosure terms.

options.label: Binary distribution
options.description: Distributing compiled binaries

options.label: SaaS deployment
options.description: Making the software available as a service

options.label: Internal use by large organizations
options.description: Use within large organizations with many employees

options.label: Commercial use
options.description: Any use for commercial purposes

questions.title: What is the timeline for source code disclosure?
questions.description: Specify the time frame within which source code must be made available after a triggering event.
questions.tooltip: A reasonable disclosure timeline balances licensor protection with licensee flexibility.
questions.help_text: 30 to 90 days are common disclosure timelines in copyleft licenses.
questions.legal_implications: Unreasonably short timelines may be unenforceable; overly long timelines reduce protection.

options.label: Immediately
options.description: Source must be available at the time of distribution

options.label: Within 30 days
options.description: Source must be disclosed within 30 days

options.label: Within 90 days
options.description: Source must be disclosed within 90 days

options.label: Within one year
options.description: Source must be disclosed within one year

questions.title: Where must disclosed source code be hosted?
questions.description: Specify the requirements for where source code must be made available when disclosure is required.
questions.tooltip: Accessible hosting ensures that source code remains available to the community.
questions.help_text: Consider whether a public repository, company website, or any URL is acceptable.
questions.legal_implications: Source hosted at an inaccessible location may not satisfy disclosure requirements.

options.label: Public repository
options.description: Must be available on a public code hosting platform

options.label: Company website
options.description: Can be hosted on the distributor's website

options.label: Any accessible URL
options.description: Any URL that is publicly accessible

options.label: Physical media on request
options.description: Source available on physical media for cost of distribution

questions.title: Is static linking to this software permitted?
questions.description: Determine whether other software can be statically linked (compiled together) with this software.
questions.tooltip: Static linking creates a single executable and raises questions about derivative works.
questions.help_text: GPL-family licenses consider static linking as creating a derivative work; permissive licenses do not.
questions.legal_implications: If static linking creates a derivative work, the combined work may need to be licensed under the same terms.

questions.title: Does static linking create a derivative work?
questions.description: Define whether statically linking with this software creates a derivative work that must be licensed under the same terms.
questions.tooltip: This is one of the most debated questions in open-source licensing.
questions.help_text: The FSF considers static linking as creating a derivative work; others disagree. Be explicit.
questions.legal_implications: Ambiguity on this point leads to widespread non-compliance and legal uncertainty in the ecosystem.

questions.title: What license propagation requirements apply for static linking?
questions.description: Specify what licensing obligations apply to the combined work when static linking occurs.
questions.tooltip: License propagation terms determine how license obligations flow to statically linked code.
questions.help_text: Consider whether to require the same license, a compatible license, or no propagation at all.
questions.legal_implications: Incompatible license propagation requirements can prevent static linking with proprietary software entirely.

options.label: No license propagation
options.description: Linked code retains its own license

options.label: Same license required
options.description: The entire work must be under this license

options.label: Compatible license required
options.description: The linked code must use a compatible license

options.label: LGPL-style linking exception
options.description: Linked work can use any license if the library remains under this license

questions.title: Is object code disclosure required for statically linked works?
questions.description: Determine whether licensees must provide the intermediate object code when static linking triggers source disclosure.
questions.tooltip: Object code disclosure is sometimes required as an alternative to full source code disclosure.
questions.help_text: This is common in LGPL licenses where the library source must be available but the application does not.
questions.legal_implications: Object code requirements can be a reasonable compromise between source disclosure and proprietary use.

questions.title: Is dynamic linking to this software permitted?
questions.description: Determine whether other software can dynamically link (load at runtime) with this software.
questions.tooltip: Dynamic linking keeps the two programs separate at runtime through shared libraries.
questions.help_text: Most licenses allow dynamic linking; the key question is whether it creates a derivative work.
questions.legal_implications: Restricting dynamic linking can severely limit the software's usability as a library.

questions.title: Does dynamic linking create a derivative work?
questions.description: Define whether dynamically linking with this software creates a derivative work that must inherit the license.
questions.tooltip: The derivative work question is generally considered less controversial for dynamic linking than static.
questions.help_text: Most legal scholars consider dynamic linking less likely to create a derivative work than static linking.
questions.legal_implications: Explicitly addressing this question eliminates legal ambiguity for downstream developers.

questions.title: What license obligations apply to dynamically linked code?
questions.description: Specify the license terms that apply to code that dynamically links with this software.
questions.tooltip: License obligations for dynamic linking are typically lighter than for static linking.
questions.help_text: Consider whether the linking application must use the same license or can use any license.
questions.legal_implications: License propagation through dynamic linking is a contentious issue that should be explicitly addressed.

options.label: No license propagation
options.description: The application retains its own license

options.label: Same license required
options.description: The application must use this license

options.label: Notice and attribution
options.description: Must include license notice and attribution

questions.title: Is API/interface stability guaranteed for dynamic linking?
questions.description: Determine whether the licensor commits to maintaining a stable API for dynamic linking compatibility.
questions.tooltip: API stability guarantees help downstream developers who depend on dynamic linking.
questions.help_text: API stability is important for library-type software where others depend on the interface.
questions.legal_implications: Promising API stability without delivering it could lead to claims of misrepresentation.

questions.title: Does providing the software over a network constitute distribution?
questions.description: Decide whether making the software available over a network (e.g., SaaS, cloud services) counts as distribution that triggers license obligations.
questions.tooltip: This is the 'SaaS loophole' question that AGPL was created to address.
questions.help_text: GPL/AGPL differ on this point: AGPL closes the SaaS loophole; GPL does not.
questions.legal_implications: The answer to this question fundamentally changes the license's behavior in cloud environments.

questions.title: What network use restrictions apply?
questions.description: Select the restrictions that apply when the software is accessed or used over a network.
questions.tooltip: Network restrictions can prevent competitors from offering the software as a service without contributing back.
questions.help_text: Consider both commercial and non-commercial network use scenarios.
questions.legal_implications: Network use restrictions must be clearly defined to be enforceable.

options.label: Attribution required
options.description: Must display attribution to users over the network

options.label: Source disclosure required
options.description: Must provide source code to network users

options.label: Notification to licensor
options.description: Must notify the licensor of network deployment

options.label: No network restrictions
options.description: Network use is unrestricted

questions.title: How are API interactions classified?
questions.description: Determine whether API calls to a service using this software constitute use, distribution, or network access under the license.
questions.tooltip: API interaction classification affects whether API consumers have license obligations.
questions.help_text: This is important for microservices architectures where components communicate via APIs.
questions.legal_implications: Misclassifying API interactions can create unexpected license obligations for API consumers.

options.label: Not distribution or use
options.description: API calls do not trigger license obligations

options.label: Constitutes use
options.description: API callers are considered users of the software

options.label: Constitutes distribution
options.description: API interactions are treated as distribution

questions.title: Is network interaction logging required?
questions.description: Specify whether the licensor must be notified of or provided with logs of network interactions with the software.
questions.tooltip: Logging requirements can provide usage data but raise privacy concerns.
questions.help_text: Logging is more common in enterprise licenses than in open-source licenses.
questions.legal_implications: Mandatory logging requirements may conflict with data protection regulations like GDPR.

questions.title: Is binary distribution of the software permitted?
questions.description: Determine whether licensees can distribute compiled binaries of the software to third parties.
questions.tooltip: Binary distribution allows the software to reach users who cannot compile from source.
questions.help_text: Most licenses allow binary distribution, but some restrictions may apply.
questions.legal_implications: Restricting binary distribution limits the software's accessibility and adoption.

questions.title: What conditions apply to distribution?
questions.description: Select the conditions that must be met when distributing the software or derivative works.
questions.tooltip: Distribution conditions define what obligations accompany redistribution.
questions.help_text: Common conditions include license inclusion, source availability, and attribution.
questions.legal_implications: Clear distribution conditions prevent downstream non-compliance and license violations.

options.label: License text must be included
options.description: A copy of the license must accompany the distribution

options.label: Attribution required
options.description: Must credit the original author(s)

options.label: Source code must be available
options.description: Source code must be provided with or alongside the binary

options.label: No conditions
options.description: Distribution is unrestricted

questions.title: Must the license be included in all distributions?
questions.description: Determine whether a copy of the license text must accompany every distribution of the software.
questions.tooltip: License inclusion ensures that all recipients are aware of their rights and obligations.
questions.help_text: This is a standard requirement in virtually all open-source licenses.
questions.legal_implications: Omitting the license text from distributions can void the license grant for recipients.

questions.title: Are there restrictions on distribution media?
questions.description: Specify whether the distribution medium (electronic, physical, etc.) is restricted.
questions.tooltip: Medium restrictions can affect how the software reaches end users.
questions.help_text: Most modern licenses do not restrict distribution medium.
questions.legal_implications: Medium restrictions may be difficult to enforce in the digital age.

options.label: Any medium permitted
options.description: Electronic and physical distribution allowed

options.label: Electronic only
options.description: Distribution limited to electronic means

options.label: Physical media only
options.description: Distribution limited to physical media like USB, CD, DVD

questions.title: Is modification of the software allowed?
questions.description: Determine whether licensees can modify the source code and create derivative works.
questions.tooltip: Modification rights are fundamental to the open-source model.
questions.help_text: Restricting modification makes the software effectively closed-source regardless of source availability.
questions.legal_implications: Restricting modification is incompatible with the Open Source Definition and OSI approval.

questions.title: Must modifications to the software be disclosed?
questions.description: Decide whether modifications must be shared back with the community or made publicly available.
questions.tooltip: Mandatory disclosure of modifications is a core copyleft principle.
questions.help_text: Permissive licenses do not require disclosure; copyleft licenses do.
questions.legal_implications: Mandatory disclosure requirements significantly limit how organizations can use the software internally.

questions.title: What naming requirements apply to modified versions?
questions.description: Specify whether modified versions must use a different name to avoid confusion with the original.
questions.tooltip: Naming requirements prevent confusion between the original and modified versions.
questions.help_text: This protects the original project's reputation if the modified version has issues.
questions.legal_implications: Failure to rename modified versions can lead to trademark infringement claims.

options.label: Must use different name
options.description: Modified versions must have a distinct name

options.label: Must indicate modification
options.description: Must clearly indicate the version is modified

options.label: No naming restrictions
options.description: Modified versions can use the original name

questions.title: Are modifications subject to review or approval?
questions.description: Determine whether modifications must be reviewed and approved before they can be distributed or used publicly.
